title: Azure Overprivileged Managed Policy Attachment

compliance.assurance_rationale: Saved search evidence for AU-2 when alert outputs are archived.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `azure:monitor:activity` events with `eventName="AttachUserPolicy" OR eventName="AttachRolePolicy"` into `index=azure`. Confirm UC-4.4.62 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `azure:monitor:activity` traffic without `eventName="AttachUserPolicy" OR eventName="AttachRolePolicy"`. Confirm UC-4.4.62 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`azure:monitor:activity` collected via Splunk cloud TA for Azure; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

description: UC-4.4.62 — Azure Overprivileged Managed Policy Attachment: queries Microsoft Azure `azure:monitor:activity` for `AttachUserPolicy`, `AttachRolePolicy` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, attaching broad managed policies via 'Azure Overprivileged Managed Policy Attachment' violates least privilege and enables lateral movement if those credentials are phished or leaked. UC-4.4.62 drives high-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=azure sourcetype=azure:monitor:activity.
visualization: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report.
knownFalsePositives: Approved change windows; documented automation service principals; sandbox accounts excluded via lookup.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure Splunk cloud TA for Azure with the modular input for `azure:monitor:activity`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `operationName` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=azure sourcetype=azure:monitor:activity.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="azure:monitor:activity" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="azure:monitor:activity" eventName="AttachUserPolicy" OR eventName="AttachRolePolicy"
| table _time operationName caller resourceId resultType
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.62_azure_overprivileged_man_62"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `azure:monitor:activity` in `index=azure` to detect azure overprivileged managed policy attachment. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Azure portal Activity Log blade for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `operationName` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_62_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk cloud TA for Azure and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure overprivileged managed policy attachment so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
